notes: Conjecture true: every row n >= 3 has at least n n-digit multiples of n with digit sum n. n <= 130 by digit DP; for n >= 131 an EGZ solution with digits <= 2 (Lean: A084029_row_nonempty) plus 2^(Z/3) unit moves i -> i -+ ord_m(10) when 2 ord <= n-1-e, and for n = p^k with 10 a primitive root the pair family 2e_0 + e_t + sum (e_i + e_(i+h)) giving C((n-1)/2,2) >= n solutions. Outside Lean: the two counting arguments (paper, checked numerically for 131 <= n <= 200) and the Python DP for n <= 130.
